newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds rise, seen treading water.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds rise, seen treading water.

text.p: Argentine bonds were higher late Monday after a session of calm activity tracking U.S. Treasuries.
Traders said the market followed U.S. Treasuries faithfully upwards but added that the market's direction remains basically flat.
"The market is treading water - this is just traders' action," said one player.
Argentina's FRB Brady bond due 2005 was up 1/4 at 89-5/8, while the dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 rose $0.10 to 127.40.
With last week's U.S. unemployment report not having ended the uncertainty over U.S. rates, players think there is little scope for the market to break out of its trading ranges.
"The market's uncertainty may not end until the next meeting" of the U.S. policy-setting Federal Open Market Committee, said another trader.
With another potential rate hike hanging over the market, traders said activity remained thin with investors neither willing to exit from their positions nor take on new ones.
In the money markets, call money rates fell to 5.98 percent from 6.03 percent.
